crisis.label: Severe
crisis.detail: Aug 4: The Aug 1-2 strike stand-down holds into a third day, but confidence in Trump's 'imminent' deal cracked. Iran's Foreign Ministry denied direct US-Iran talks are underway, saying it is negotiating exclusively with Oman over a 'temporary' safe shipping corridor rather than a full reopening, and vowed the Strait 'will in no way return to the status it was before February 28th' (Fox News, Aug 3). A source close to Iran's negotiating team separately denied any reopening agreement has been reached (APA, Aug 2). A tanker was struck by an unknown projectile about 20nm northeast of Al Khasab, Oman on Monday, damaging its engine room; no casualties (UKMTO via Gulf News, Aug 3). Kpler data published Aug 3 shows Hormuz crossings rose 8% week-on-week (Jul 27-Aug 2, averaging about 15/day) with 3 LNG tanker transits in the week - the first LNG-specific movement since the July 18 zero-transit observation. Oil steadied near Monday's lower levels: Brent +0.8% to $84.28, WTI +1.8% to $80.84 (Trading Economics, Aug 4). Tail raised to 47% as Iran's denial of a full deal and the fresh tanker strike temper Saturday's optimism.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Trump's Aug 1-2 strike stand-down holds and Oman-mediated talks eventually convert into a phased reopening, but Iran's Aug 3 denial of a full deal and insistence on only a 'temporary' corridor lengthens the timeline. Probability trimmed because the 'imminent' framing from Aug 1-2 has not been confirmed by Iran's own statements.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: Talks continue but remain stuck on Iran's insistence on a Oman-mediated 'temporary' corridor rather than a full reopening; sporadic incidents persist, illustrated by Monday's unknown-projectile strike on a tanker off Oman even as large-scale strikes stay paused. Hormuz traffic ticks up (Kpler: about 15/day, +8% w/w) but remains far below the roughly 88/day pre-war norm.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: The stand-down proves as fragile as the Jul 26-30 pause: Iran's denial of a full reopening deal and the fresh tanker strike signal talks are stalling. A resumption of US strikes against IRGC and strategic targets, and renewed Iranian attacks across Gulf states and commercial shipping, would send Brent back toward $105-135+/bbl and JKM above $30/MMBtu.

priceNarratives.Brent: Pre-shock ~$65 -> $126 wartime high intraday (Day 59, Apr 30, CNBC/CNN) -> $98.57 (Jun 3 D93 peak) -> $90.12 (Aug 1, Yahoo Finance BZ=F) as tanker incidents and Kuwait attacks kept risk elevated -> $83.61 (Aug 3, -4.9%, Investing.com) as Trump canceled planned strikes and called a Hormuz/denuclearization deal 'imminent' -> $84.28 (Aug 4, +0.8%, Trading Economics) as Iran denied a full reopening deal and a tanker was struck off Oman. Yahoo's BZ=F/CL=F/TTF=F/EURUSD=X feeds all carried a stale chartPreviousClose reference on Aug 4 (spuriously implying a further plunge), so Trading Economics is used as the confirmed source. Working range narrows to $75-90 base; $85-105 stress; $105-135+ tail.
priceNarratives.JKM LNG: Baseline $9.5 -> $23.40/MMBtu (Day 20, Reuters/Platts) -> $19.93/MMBtu (Jul 16, Trading Economics) -> $22.00/MMBtu (Jul 24, Reuters Sept-delivery assessment) as sustained Hormuz disruption tightened Asian LNG balances; carried at $22.00 pending a newer weekly assessment. Contextual CFD reference $21.26/MMBtu (Trading Economics, Aug 3, -0.91%). Qatar force majeure remains confirmed to mid-September (Reuters, Jul 23), with a further extension to mid-October reportedly in preparation (Bloomberg, Jul 22, unconfirmed).
priceNarratives.TTF Gas: Pre-shock ~$34/MWh -> 63.58/MWh (Jul 24, +2.71% vs Jul 23, MacroMicro) -> 59.07/MWh (Jul 31, +1.4%, Yahoo Finance TTF=F) as tanker incidents kept the supply-risk premium elevated -> 56.06 EUR/MWh (Aug 3, -5.1%, Trading Economics) as Trump's strike stand-down eased the risk premium -> 58.12 EUR/MWh (Aug 4, +3.7%, Trading Economics) as Iran's denial of a full deal reintroduced some risk premium. The marker remains elevated versus the pre-crisis baseline on persistent Qatar LNG disruption.
priceNarratives.Credit: iTraxx Asia IG est. ~140bp (Aug 4, +2bp); ASEAN HY est. ~483bp (+5bp) as Iran's denial of a full Hormuz deal and Monday's tanker strike pared back a sliver of Aug 1-3's relief rally. Tail raised to 47% while the strait remains physically closed and Kpler's Aug 3 data shows the first sustained LNG-specific Hormuz transits (3/week) since mid-July.
